headline: Solid underwriting, but profit slips on cat losses
summary_short: After-tax operating EPS was $2.67 versus $2.77 a year ago, with a combined ratio of 82.5% (79.8% a year ago). Arch repurchased $1.4B of shares in the quarter.
summary_long: Net premiums earned fell 6.3% to $4.0B as reinsurance (-10.3%) and mortgage (-10.3%) shrank. Catastrophe losses of $234M, including Iran-conflict losses, lifted the loss ratio to 55.0% from 51.4%; the expense ratio improved to 27.5% on Bermuda tax credits. Prior-year reserve releases were $179M. Net investment income rose to $451M. Buybacks of $1.4B cut diluted shares to 341.4M from 376.1M. Book value per share was $67.90.
confidence_notes: Operating EPS is a non-GAAP measure as defined in the release; y/y deltas use the release's own prior-year figures ($2.77 operating EPS, $1,340M net income). No numeric guidance issued in the release.

drivers.explanation: Higher catastrophe losses (including Iran-conflict losses) lifted the loss ratio, partly offset by a lower expense ratio helped by Bermuda qualified refundable tax credits.
Reflects changes in net premiums written over the prior five quarters; reinsurance saw non-renewals and share reductions, mortgage saw lower credit risk transfer premiums.
Lower earned premium and a higher loss ratio, partly offset by a lower expense ratio.
CEO describes a transitioning market with increasingly uneven conditions and cites solid underwriting across three segments and investment portfolio strength.
